1. Section 4. Routing and escalation policy v1. Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE.

Failing wording: "age_days since last_verdict_utc", "eff_lb95 = w * lb95 + (1 - w) * 0.5", "Decay only demotes; freshness is re-earned by new verdicts", and "n >= n_min (DEFAULT 20) AND pass_rate_lb95 >= threshold (DEFAULT 0.85, caller-overridable; v0 constant kept)."

The decay clock is last_verdict_utc, not per-verdict age. Section 3.4 writes a verdict for every gated step. Section 4.2 says every exploration answer that can be G0-gated MUST be gated. The cheapest qualifier in section 4.1 therefore keeps last_verdict_utc fresh by being chosen. w stays near 1 on every hot cell. T4 (eff_lb95 below threshold while raw lb95 is still at or above threshold) cannot fire on the cells the router is actually using. Section 8 F2's residual, "window up to half_life_days", is false for those cells. A forced probe then cancels T4 outright: k = DEFAULT 5 verdicts set age to 0, so eff_lb95 snaps back to raw lb95, which T4 itself requires to be at or above threshold. One probe round restores a cell whose mass can be the F-S1 "order 300" history. half_life_days DEFAULT 14.0 never binds steady-state G0 traffic.

The blend is not a demotion. At age = half_life, w = 0.5, so eff_lb95 = 0.5 * lb95 + 0.25. For lb95 = 0.30 that is 0.40, an increase. Amendment 4 item 3 wins over section 4.1 and demands the opposite: "with no new verdicts, eff_lb95 is non-increasing in age", "fresh forced-probe verdicts never lower eff_lb95", and "never above the raw lb95". A failing probe lowers p and can lower eff_lb95. When lb95 < 0.5 the blend sits above raw lb95. The first-test wave in AMENDMENT 4 cannot pass against the formula the same spec says to run.

The advertised qualification boundary is empty. Section 2's Wilson formula at p = 1 reduces to lb95 = n / (n + z^2) with z = 1.96, so z^2 = 3.8416. At n = 20, lb95 = 0.8389, which is below 0.85. Any fail lowers it further. n = 21 peaks at 0.8453. First perfect cell that can qualify is n = 22 (0.8513). Section 8 F3's "n_min = 20 fast graduation" is false under the defaults. Amendment 1 (wins over section 4.3) talks about a "routing-qualified cell" with "n_min <= n < m" and a dead-code window "verdicts 20 through 49". At the default threshold that window does not open at 20 or 21.

Trigger precedence is missing while the receipt field is single-valued: "none|T1_confidence|T2_economics|T3_blind_spot|T4_staleness". T3 says n < n_min climbs. T4 says "do NOT climb". Amendment 1 says a cell with n < n_min and low confidence "routes to T4 exactly as before." Fixture the spec does not decide: n = 10, confidence 0.2, calibration_state unverified, a higher tier with n >= 22 exists. Climb, ship stale, and ship low_evidence are all licensed.

2. Section 2. Ledger schema v1. Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE.

Failing wording: "PRIMARY KEY (model_id, task_shape, task_shape_version)", the Wilson block that uses unbound "p" and "n", "capability is a MATERIALIZATION of verdict, rebuildable by replay", and "UNIQUE (receipt_ref, gate_id)" plus a non-unique "ix_verdict_evidence".

Section 3.3 damns the key in the spec's own words: "A verdict is a statement about a (model, task_shape_version, environment) triple. Anything less is a vibe about a brand." Environment is "model tag, prompt template, temperature" (section 3.3). None of prompt template or temperature is in the capability key or in section 5 considered[] ({model_id, n, lb95, eff_lb95, cost, qualifies, reason_code}). Twenty temperature-0 passes and twenty temperature-1 fails on one model_id and task_shape_version land in one cell. The router then reads that pool. Section 8 F4 says environment hashes "make drift visible" and "visible is not prevented". Visibility in evidence_hash does not split the routing key.

Wilson "used everywhere" never binds p or n to the columns defined in the same CREATE TABLE. passes and fails are "WEIGHTED". sample_size is "raw verdict count". pass_rate_raw is the "weighted running mean". Section 3.1 sets weights G0 1.0, G1 1.0, G2 0.5, G3 0.25, and "sample_size counts raw verdicts". Section 4.1's "n >= n_min" does not say which n. Raw n = 20 with weighted p treats a G2-heavy cell as 20 binomial trials. Weighted n makes n_min a different gate. Both readings fit the text. Qualification is not a function of this spec.

Replay byte-identity is false on the DDL the amendment claims to reproduce. Amendment 4 item 4 (wins) says rebuilding capability by replay "reproduces the live rows exactly." Section 9 says cost_usd_last is "operator or fixture written". half_life_days is a mutable column (DEFAULT 14.0), not a verdict field. quarantined is an audit side effect. An UPDATE of half_life_days to 1e9 on one cell disables section 4.1 decay with no signature and no chain row. Replay cannot regenerate that UPDATE. The audit promise and the first-test wave disagree with the schema.

The idempotency key stops same (receipt_ref, gate_id) only. A second receipt_ref with the same evidence_hash increments passes, fails, and sample_size. Section 7 K5 calls "replay double-counted" a contract failure. Section 8 F5's defense is the non-unique evidence index plus unspecified "near-duplicate input clustering". Detection is not a reject. The v0 hole named in section 3.2 (verdicts without receipts) is relocated, not closed.

3. Section 7. Acceptance harness. Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE.

Failing wording: "M2 verified-solve rate (kill rule, not a powered claim at n = 200)" beside "K2 Arm 1 solve rate > 3 points below Arm 2 (ESTIMATE threshold visible at n = 200) => kill regardless of cost", and "ARM 1 ALSO CARRIES amortized probe + seed-corpus + audit spend from probe_log and M5" beside "K1 Arm 1 not >= 10% better than BOTH Arm 2 and Arm 3 on M1 with paired 95% CI excluding zero".

Section 0 grants routing authority only by "passing the acceptance harness (section 7)". K2 is a kill on a gap the same section says is not powered at the only n it names. No base rate is given, so this is not a spec-stated SE, but the internal pair is enough: an unpowered 3-point rule at n = 200 both false-kills and false-spares. K1's 10% is not a predicate until an amortization horizon and an eval n exist. Neither is in section 7. Seed-corpus plus probe_log spend divided by 200 items and the same spend divided by a year of traffic can flip K1. The implementer picks the window. That is an unfalsifiable grant button.

Section 6 says "each is falsifiable and the acceptance harness measures every one" of F-S1 through F-S7. Section 7's instruments are M1 through M6 and K1 through K5. No kill measures F-S1 (order 300 inside one half-life), F-S2 (>= 10x stable price), F-S3 (top 5 shapes >= 80% of traffic), or F-S5 (half-life exceeds accumulation time). F-S4, called "THE crux", is assigned to M6, and M6 is "ECE per model per shape". ECE is not "per-instance confidence cannot catch it but the population rate would." A calibrated model can still be confidently wrong on a subclass. F-S6 ("gate cost per cascade instance <= ~10% (ESTIMATE)") has no named comparator or kill. F-S2 damns itself: "fixtures are literals, not measurements", section 7 measures "routing quality at fixture prices, not frontier economics", and section 4.1 constrains on "live config price, never ledger price". A K1 pass at fixture 30x does not license authority on the clock that actually routes. Arm 4 FIXED-MID is outside K1, so a ledger worse than the floor on M1 still takes authority if it beats Arm 2 and Arm 3.

Missing predicates, by damage if absent:

1. Pinned qualification witness. Belongs next to section 2 (Wilson block) and section 4.1 item 2. The spec must publish p, n, and the qualify bit for at least two vectors, to 1e-6 on lb95. Vector A: 20 G0 passes, weights 1.0, sample_size 20, threshold 0.85, half_life irrelevant at age 0. Under the printed Wilson formula lb95 = 0.8389 and the qualify bit is false, so the defaults have no witness at n_min. Vector B: 1 G2 pass (weight 0.5) plus 19 G3 passes (weight 0.25), sample_size 20. The spec must name n and must set the qualify bit false unless G0+G1+G2 weight sum is at least 10. Falsifying measurement: any implementation whose qualify bit or lb95 differs from the pin, or a spec that still has no pin, fails. Amendment 4 item 2 currently flips qualification on exactly one non-G3 verdict, which is the hole Vector B is there to close.

2. Environment partition. Belongs next to section 2 PRIMARY KEY, section 3.3, and section 5 considered[]. Falsifying measurement: 20 G0 passes at temperature 0.0 and 20 G0 fails at temperature 1.0, same model_id, task_shape, task_shape_version, distinct prompt-template ids inside the section 3.3 environment hash. A route whose call temperature is 1.0 must see n and lb95 from the temperature-1 rows only, must not qualify, and the receipt considered[] entry must record the environment key used. Pooled n = 40 or a qualify bit of true fails the test. Whether tools/gps_mcp/seed_fixtures.py is single-environment is UNPROVEN from this text; section 7 only says the split is "deterministic per tools/gps_mcp/seed_fixtures.py patterns".

3. Single new verdict must not restore a decayed cell. Belongs next to section 4.1 and section 4.4. Falsifying measurement: 300 G0 passes, raw lb95 above 0.85, each verdict ts_utc = now minus 28 days (two times half_life_days DEFAULT 14.0), zero newer verdicts. Record eff_lb95. Insert one passing G0 probe at now. eff_lb95 must remain below 0.85, and the weight on the 300 old verdicts must not jump from the decayed weight to 1. The section 4.1 last_verdict_utc rule fails this by construction. Second fixture: lb95 = 0.30 at age 0 and at age 14 days; eff_lb95(14) must be <= eff_lb95(0). The printed blend yields 0.30 then 0.40.

4. Ungated low-confidence stops block qualification. Belongs next to section 3.4 and section 4.1 item 2. Falsifying measurement: on one (model_id, task_shape, task_shape_version), 20 G0 pass verdicts and 80 receipt rows with confidence below min_confidence DEFAULT 0.8, stopped for LOW CONFIDENCE, no verdict, same trace population. Qualify bit must be false. The spec as written qualifies the cell (n = 20, p = 1, section 3.4 writes nothing for the stops). A cheap model that abstains on hard items wins "cheapest qualifying" and improves M1 by never paying a fail. No section 8 row covers this.

5. Same evidence under a new receipt must not move aggregates. Belongs next to section 2 UNIQUE (receipt_ref, gate_id), section 8 F5, and section 7 K5. Falsifying measurement: commit one passing verdict, then insert a second row with a new receipt_ref, new verdict_id, and the same evidence_hash (same input bytes, answer bytes, checker id+version, environment). The insert must be rejected, or passes, fails, sample_size, pass_rate_lb95 must stay byte-identical. sample_size becoming 2 fails. Amendment 4 item 4 only replays the same verdict_id and the same (receipt_ref, gate_id). K5 names "replay double-counted" and does not define replay as this pair.

### PART 1: THREE WEAKEST SECTIONS (Ranked by Damage)

#### Rank 1: Section 4.1 (Selection - router reads ONLY these)
- Verdict: KILL
- Exact wording or default that fails:
  `eff_lb95 = w * lb95 + (1 - w) * 0.5` where `w = exp(-ln2 * age_days / half_life_days)` alongside the qualifier condition: `eff_lb95 >= threshold (DEFAULT 0.85)`.
- Evidence inside the spec text that damns it:
  1. Mathematical impossibility on qualification: Section 4.1 states that if `eff_lb95 < threshold`, the cell does not qualify. If none qualify, Section 4.1 states: "route cheapest constraint-passing AND schedule a forced probe round... on the stalest rows." But when `w` decays, `eff_lb95` pulls toward the uninformative prior `p0 = 0.5`. Because the default threshold is 0.85, any cell that stops receiving continuous traffic rapidly drops below 0.85 (in less than half a half-life, approximately 4.3 days for a perfect 1.0 lb95 cell with half_life_days = 14.0).
  2. Direct conflict with Section 4.3 T4 STALENESS: Section 4.3 explicitly defines T4 as: "eff_lb95 < threshold while raw lb95 >= threshold (decay demotion): do NOT climb; ship current-tier answer flagged stale: true and schedule the forced probe." 
  However, Section 4.1 disqualifies this cell at step 3 (`eff_lb95 >= threshold`) before escalation logic in Section 4.3 can ever execute. Section 4.1 states "router reads ONLY these" and filters candidates out of the candidate qualification pool. Therefore, a stale model is rejected by Section 4.1, preventing Section 4.3 T4 from ever executing on that tier. The router either climbs to an un-decayed expensive tier (violating Section 4.3: "frontier tokens never patch measurement holes") or drops to "route cheapest constraint-passing" in Section 4.1, making the T4 escalation trigger dead code.

#### Rank 2: Amendment 2 (kill 2: chain concurrency and fork story; amends 2 and 9)
- Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE
- Exact wording or default that fails:
  `longest-valid-chain-wins: losing-branch verdicts are quarantined, never deleted (append-only law), capability rows rebuild by replay`
- Evidence inside the spec text that damns it:
  1. Contradiction of single-writer concurrency guarantee: Amendment 2 asserts in its first sentence: "The concurrency story is: one writer, serialized transactions... contention delays, never forks." If transactions are serialized with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on a single-writer SQLite database, forks are structurally impossible within the database engine. Admitting a "longest-valid-chain-wins" rule proves the spec allows detached, partitioned, or out-of-band writers.
  2. Systematic capability corruption via orphaned valid receipts: In an append-only system where receipts bind to verdicts (`UNIQUE (receipt_ref, gate_id)` in Section 2 DDL), "longest-chain" reorganization means a legitimate, non-collusive execution step recorded in a valid receipt will have its verdict quarantined simply because an adversary or race submitted an alternative branch with length N+1.
  3. Violation of Section 0 INSTRUMENT GUARANTEE: The spec guarantees that "The ledger, gates, and receipts are valuable even if every kill rule fires... No eval outcome deletes the instrument". Silently orphaning and quarantining valid verdicts via Nakamoto-style longest-chain selection destroys receipt auditability and allows an attacker to erase low-score verdicts on a favored model by spamming a longer chain of cheap G0 assertions on another cell.

#### Rank 3: Section 3.1 & Section 2 DDL (Wilson Bound with Weighted Aggregates)
- Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE
- Exact wording or default that fails:
  `lb95: Wilson 95% lower bound on the weighted pass-rate` combined with Section 2 DDL:
  ```sql
  passes REAL NOT NULL, -- WEIGHTED pass count (s3 weights)
  fails REAL NOT NULL, -- weighted fail count
  sample_size INTEGER NOT NULL, -- raw verdict count
  ```
  and the Section 2 Wilson formula using `p = passes / (passes + fails)` and `n = sample_size`.
- Evidence inside the spec text that damns it:
  1. Broken statistical math: Section 3.1 assigns weights: G0=1.0, G1=1.0, G2=0.5, G3=0.25. Section 2 uses raw verdict count `sample_size` for `n` in the Wilson score interval formula:
  `half = z * sqrt(p*(1-p)/n + z*z/(4*n*n)) / (1 + z*z/n)`.
  If a cell has 100 G3 verdicts (weight 0.25) with 100 passes, `passes = 25.0`, `fails = 0.0`, `sample_size = 100`. The code computes `p = 25/25 = 1.0` with `n = 100`. The Wilson bound calculated understates the variance because the effective degrees of freedom (effective sample size per Kish's formula) is far smaller than raw sample size.
  2. Direct conflict with Amendment 4 Predicate 3: Amendment 4 Predicate 3 asserts: "fresh forced-probe verdicts never lower eff_lb95; a probe round on a decayed cell restores eff_lb95 monotonically along the 4.1 arithmetic and never above the raw lb95 the same evidence supports."
  If a cell has 20 G0 passes (`passes = 20, n = 20, lb95 = 0.838`), adding a G2 pass (`weight = 0.5`) increments `passes` to 20.5 and increments `sample_size` to 21. If `n` increments by 1.0 while weight only increments by 0.5, the denominator in `n` grows faster than weighted success, creating artificial non-monotonic perturbations in `lb95`. The Wilson interval is mathematically undefined for fractional binomial trials without an effective sample size correction (`n_eff = (sum w)^2 / sum(w^2)`).

---

### PART 2: FIVE MOST IMPORTANT MISSING PREDICATES (Ranked by Damage)

#### Rank 1: Effective Sample Size Conservation Under Mixed Gate Weights
- Falsifying Measurement:
  Construct a cell with 40 G3 verdicts (all pass, weight 0.25 each, sum of weights = 10) and 1 G0 verdict (pass, weight 1.0, total sum of weights = 11, total raw n = 41). Compute `lb95` using the Section 2 formula with `n = 41` versus an exact binomial baseline of 11 independent trials with 11 passes. If the ledger's computed `lb95` produces an error greater than 0.05 against the true binomial confidence interval of 11 trials, or if adding a passing G3 verdict decreases `pass_rate_lb95`, the check FAILS.
- Section it belongs next to:
  Section 3.1 (Gate classes, evidence minimums, weights) and Section 2 (DDL Wilson bound definition).

#### Rank 2: Replay Rebuild Determinism Under Out-of-Order Receipt Ingestion
- Falsifying Measurement:
  Stream 1,000 valid verdicts into the ledger across 10 models and 5 task shapes. Export the final `capability` table state. Truncate `capability`, shuffle the 1,000 rows in `verdict` randomly, and re-execute the materialization replay engine. If the resulting `capability` table differs by even one bit in `passes`, `fails`, `pass_rate_lb95`, or `quarantined` flags from the pre-truncation state, the check FAILS.
- Section it belongs next to:
  Section 2 (Ledger schema v1 - capability materialization definition).

#### Rank 3: Calibration ECE Sample Variance and Invalidation Boundary
- Falsifying Measurement:
  Set `m_eff = n_min = 20` per Amendment 1. Inject 20 gated answers with alternating calibrated confidences (0.80) and boolean outcomes such that empirical ECE is exactly 0.09 (`<= e_max = 0.10`, marking `calibration_state = verified`). Flip the next single outcome (verdict 21) from pass to fail. If `calibration_state` does not atomically flip to `poor` or `unverified` within the same transaction, or if the router permits a T1 escalation on verdict 22 before the ECE recalculates, the check FAILS.
- Section it belongs next to:
  Section 4.3 (T1 CONFIDENCE) and Amendment 1.

#### Rank 4: Probe Budget Depletion Hard-Stop Enforcement
- Falsifying Measurement:
  Initialize a task shape with `probe_budget_usd = 0.50`. Route synthetic traffic that exhausts the $0.50 budget in `probe_log` using 5 probe executions costing $0.10 each. Submit the 6th request where all qualifying models are stale (`eff_lb95 < threshold`). If the router triggers an outbound probe call, records a new entry in `probe_log` exceeding $0.50 within the 7-day rolling window, or fails to emit a receipt with `probe: false` and `stale: true`, the check FAILS.
- Section it belongs next to:
  Section 4.4 (Probe budget) and Section 5 (Receipt-row grammar).

#### Rank 5: Operator Recusal Boundary Under Key Rotation and Alias Masquerading
- Falsifying Measurement:
  Register `operator_A` with `principal_1`. Create a task shape owned by `principal_1`. Rotate `principal_1` to `principal_2` (`rotated_from = 'principal_1'`, `operator_id = 'operator_A'`). Submit an ask via `principal_2`. Attempt to insert a G1, G2, or G3 verdict on the resulting `receipt_ref` signed by `principal_3`, where `principal_3` has `operator_id = 'operator_A'` but a distinct, non-linked `rotated_from` lineage (a sibling key in the same operator family). If the ledger write transaction accepts the verdict rather than rejecting it with an auth/recusal error, the check FAILS.
- Section it belongs next to:
  Section 3.2 (Who can write - RECUSAL RULE) and Amendment 3.

THREE WEAKEST SECTIONS, ranked by damage if unfixed.

1. Section 3.1, Gate classes, evidence minimums, weights. Verdict: KILL.
Exact wording that fails: "G3 CAP (hard rule): a cell whose verdicts are entirely G3 can never present eff_lb95 above the routing threshold; at least one G0/G1/G2 verdict is required before a cell may qualify." Also: "lb95: Wilson 95% lower bound on the weighted pass-rate" and "sample_size counts raw verdicts."
Evidence inside the spec that damns it: G3 weight is 0.25, G2 is 0.5, G0/G1 are 1.0. A cell with 1 G0 fail and 100 G3 passes has weighted pass_rate_raw = 25/(1+25) = 0.9615. With raw n=101, Wilson lb95 is approximately 0.904, which clears threshold 0.85. With effective n = 1 + 100*0.25 = 26, Wilson lb95 is approximately 0.811, which does not clear 0.85. The spec uses raw sample_size in the Wilson formula, so G3 flooding can qualify a cell despite a deterministic G0 fail. The G3 cap only requires one non-G3 verdict, not one non-G3 pass, and does not cap G3 weight share.

2. Section 4.1, Selection (router reads ONLY these). Verdict: KILL.
Exact wording that fails: "threshold (DEFAULT 0.85, caller-overridable; v0 constant kept)."
Evidence inside the spec that damns it: Section 0 says routing authority is PROVISIONAL and earned by passing the acceptance harness. Section 4.1 says the router reads ONLY these, but caller-overridable threshold lets a caller set threshold to 0.0 and route to any cell with n >= n_min, including a cell with lb95 = 0.0. Section 5 receipt-row grammar has no required field for the threshold actually used, so the override is not auditable from the receipt spine.

3. Section 6, Scope fences (pre-registration, from the adversary seat). Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE.
Exact wording that fails: "each is falsifiable and the acceptance harness measures every one."
Evidence inside the spec that damns it: Section 7 metrics are M1 through M6. None measure F-S1 verdict supply, F-S2 cost dispersion, F-S3 concentration, F-S5 drift slowness, or F-S6 gate economics. F-S4 says "harness M6 measures it," but M6 is "ECE per model per shape," which does not measure invisible-failure heterogeneity. F-S2 says "fixtures are literals, not measurements." The pre-registration claim is false as written.

FIVE MOST IMPORTANT MISSING PREDICATES, ranked by damage if unfixed.

1. Effective sample size for Wilson bound. Belongs next to Section 3.1 or Section 1 definitions.
Concrete testable check: For a cell with 1 G0 fail and 100 G3 passes, compute lb95 with n_eff = sum(weights) = 1 + 100*0.25 = 26. The cell must not qualify if lb95 < 0.85.
Falsifying measurement: Current spec uses sample_size = 101 raw, yielding lb95 approximately 0.904 >= 0.85. Effective n = 26 yields lb95 approximately 0.811 < 0.85. The test fails on current spec.

2. G3 weight share cap. Belongs next to Section 3.1 G3 CAP.
Concrete testable check: A cell with 1 G0 pass and 1000 G3 passes must not qualify if G3 weight share > 0.5 or if non-G3 pass count < 1.
Falsifying measurement: Current spec only requires at least one G0/G1/G2 verdict, so the cell qualifies with weighted pass_rate_raw = 251/251 = 1.0 and Wilson lb95 approximately 0.996. The test fails on current spec.

3. Caller-overridable threshold enforcement. Belongs next to Section 4.1.
Concrete testable check: A caller sets threshold = 0.0 and attempts to route to a cell with n = 0 or lb95 = 0.0. The router must reject or require a signed registry owner override logged in the receipt.
Falsifying measurement: Current spec says "caller-overridable," so the route succeeds. The test fails on current spec.

4. F-S4 invisible-failure heterogeneity direct test. Belongs next to Section 6 F-S4 or Section 7 M6.
Concrete testable check: On a shape where a cheap model is confidently wrong, compare per-instance confidence filter (climb if conf < 0.8) versus ledger population rate (climb if eff_lb95 < 0.85). Count items where per-instance filter passes but ledger would climb.
Falsifying measurement: M6 ECE per model per shape does not measure this. If the count is 0, F-S4 is false. If the count is > 0, F-S4 holds. Current spec has no such paired count.

5. T1 calibration audit fields. Belongs next to Section 5 Receipt-row grammar.
Concrete testable check: A receipt for a T1 climb must include ece_value, ece_window_n, e_max, min_confidence, and calibration_state.
Falsifying measurement: Section 5 required fields list lacks ece_value, ece_window_n, e_max, and min_confidence. A T1 trigger cannot be verified from the receipt spine. The test fails on current spec.

1. Section 2. Ledger schema v1 (as amended by AMENDMENT 2). Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE.

Failing default: `PRIMARY KEY (model_id, task_shape, task_shape_version)` plus the Wilson block that takes unbound `n` and `p`, while `passes`/`fails` are `REAL` weighted counts and `sample_size` is raw integer count. Also AMENDMENT 2's `longest-valid-chain-wins: losing-branch verdicts are quarantined`.

What damns it: Section 3.3 says a verdict is a statement about a `(model, task_shape_version, environment)` triple and "Anything less is a vibe about a brand." No capability column holds environment (section 3.1's G0 environment hash is model tag + prompt template id + temperature). Section 1 says `eff_lb95` is the only rate the router may read, and section 4.1 reads it off this key, so temperature and prompt-template drift share one cell. Section 3.1 sets weights 1.0 / 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25 and `pass_rate_raw = sum(w*v)/sum(w)`, but section 2 never binds Wilson `n` to `sample_size` or to `passes+fails`. Those two bindings disagree on whether a G3-heavy cell clears 0.85. Section 2 also says `capability` is a materialization "rebuildable by replay"; `half_life_days` and `cost_usd_last` are not on `verdict`, and section 4.1's `eff_lb95` depends on `half_life_days`, so replay is not determined. AMENDMENT 2 then crowns the longer valid-signed branch and quarantines the shorter one. Nothing in that rule prefers the first tip or diverse principals. A longer branch from one key wins; the honest tip is the branch that gets quarantined.

2. Section 4.3 Escalation decision boundaries (as amended by AMENDMENT 1). Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE.

Failing wording: "If calibration is unverified or poor, a low confidence triggers T4, not T1: an uncalibrated confidence number is noise wearing a uniform." T4 is defined as "do NOT climb; ship current-tier answer flagged stale: true". AMENDMENT 1: "low confidence routes to T4 exactly as before." Also "P(fail) = 1 - eff_lb95".

What damns it: Section 5's trigger enum has only `T4_staleness`, so the noise case is recorded as staleness. T3 says `n < n_min` climbs. The amendment-wins rule in the AMENDMENTS header cancels that climb whenever confidence is low. Low confidence therefore reduces escalation. Section 3.4 writes no verdict on a low-confidence stop, so that case is neither measured nor climbed. Section 4.1's fallback already routes the cheapest constraint-passing row when none qualify; section 4.4 then holds probes and "degrades to current behavior with stale flags." Unqualified routing sticks. T1's split depends on "rolling ECE" with no bins, no formula, and no rule for section 5's `confidence: null`. That comparison is not a test. T2 treats a 95% lower bound as a fail probability. `pass_rate_raw` exists and is marked audit-only. `1 - eff_lb95` is an upper-biased functional of a bound. AMENDMENT 4 item 5 requires that once `C_rework` is set, the same arithmetic climbs, so the wrong functional becomes the gated behavior. Section 6 F-S4's crux is confident wrongness, which fails `conf < 0.8` and never enters T1.

3. Section 4.1 Selection. Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE.

Failing default: `n >= n_min (DEFAULT 20) AND pass_rate_lb95 >= threshold (DEFAULT 0.85, caller-overridable` together with `eff_lb95 = w * lb95 + (1 - w) * 0.5`, "Decay only demotes", and age taken only from `last_verdict_utc`. AMENDMENT 4 item 3 requires the opposite arithmetic.

What damns it: Under section 2's formula at `p = 1`, `lb95 = 1 / (1 + z^2/n) = 20 / (20 + 3.8416) = 0.839 < 0.85`. A perfect cell cannot qualify at the stated `n_min`. First perfect qualification is `n = 22`. AMENDMENT 1's dead window "verdicts 20 through 49" is already partly impossible under those defaults. For a 0.90 cell, qualification starts near `n = 200`, which is already above `m = 50`, so the T1 rewrite does not open the gap F-S4 cells actually sit in. ### Three Weakest Sections of the Spec

Ranked by damage if unfixed:

#### 1. AMENDMENT 3 (kill 3: enforceable recusal; amends 2 principal DDL and 3.2)
* Verdict: KILL
* Exact wording that fails:

* Evidence inside spec text that damns it:

Section 1 explicitly states: "Endpoints and models are never principals and never write verdicts about themselves." By resolving the operator of a model from the `principal_ids` on receipts where that model was chosen, Amendment 3 defines the *caller* of an API as the *operator* of the external model. If the estate operator (`operator_id = 'estate'`) routes work to a model, the estate operator is permanently classified as the operator of that model cell, barring the estate from ever submitting G2 human operator judgments on its own routed traffic under Section 3.2. Simultaneously, an external model provider who never submits routing asks has zero receipt entries and can submit G3 verdicts on its own models without triggering recusal.

#### 2. Section 3.1 (Gate classes, evidence minimums, weights)
* Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE
* Exact wording that fails:
  `G3 CAP (hard rule): a cell whose verdicts are entirely G3 can never present eff_lb95 above the routing threshold; at least one G0/G1/G2 verdict is required before a cell may qualify. Weighted update: pass_rate_raw = sum(w*v)/sum(w); passes/fails accumulate weights; sample_size counts raw verdicts; gate_class_mix exposes composition.`
* Evidence inside spec text that damns it:
  The DDL in Section 2 defines `sample_size` as the raw verdict count and feeds it directly into the Wilson lower bound formula:
  `half = z * sqrt(p*(1-p)/n + z*z/(4*n*n)) / (1 + z*z/n)`
  Plugging the raw count `sample_size` into $n$ while calculating $p$ from weights where G3 has weight 0.25 violates binomial distribution assumptions. A cell with 400 G3 verdicts has an effective sample size of 100, but using $n = 400$ artificially deflates the variance width `half` by half ($\sqrt{1/4}$), fabricating unearned statistical confidence. Furthermore, the G3 cap rule states: "at least one G0/G1/G2 verdict is required before a cell may qualify." It does not require that this anchor verdict be a PASS. An attacker can write 200 passing G3 model-judge verdicts and 1 failing G0 test verdict; the cell now has a non-G3 verdict, raw sample size 201, weighted pass rate $50 / 51 = 0.980$, and an inflated `lb95` above the 0.85 qualification threshold. The cap is completely bypassed by a single failed gate.

#### 3. Section 4.1 (Selection, router reads ONLY these)
* Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE
* Exact wording that fails:
  `eff_lb95 = w * lb95 + (1 - w) * 0.5 with age_days since last_verdict_utc, p0 = 0.5 pessimistic prior. Decay only demotes; freshness is re-earned by new verdicts`
* Evidence inside spec text that damns it:
  The assertion "Decay only demotes" is mathematically false whenever `lb95 < 0.5`. If a failing model cell has 20 verdicts with a 10% pass rate, its Wilson lower bound is `lb95 = 0.026`. As `age_days` increases, the decay weight $w \to 0$, causing `eff_lb95` to trend toward the prior `p0 = 0.5`. At two half-lives ($w = 0.25$), `eff_lb95 = 0.25*(0.026) + 0.75*(0.5) = 0.3815`. The formula promotes failing cells from 0.026 to 0.3815 simply through the passage of time. Blending an interval boundary (`lb95`) with a point probability prior (`0.5`) is statistically invalid. This arithmetic also conflicts with Amendment 4 Item 3, which claims "fresh forced-probe verdicts never lower eff_lb95", an impossible property if a forced probe returns a failing verdict.

### Weakest Sections (Ranked by Damage if Unfixed)

#### Rank 1: AMENDMENT 2 (kill 2: chain concurrency and fork story)
- Verdict: KILL
- Exact wording that fails: "In production the periodic audit (replay from genesis, recomputing every hash link) resolves any detected fork by longest-valid-chain-wins: losing-branch verdicts are quarantined, never deleted (append-only law), capability rows rebuild by replay"
- Damning evidence: Section 9 explicitly establishes "single writer SQLite", and AMENDMENT 2 enforces "one writer, serialized transactions" via `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. In an authenticated single-writer ledger, a fork is not a distributed network partition: it is either local corruption or an active key compromise. Applying Nakamoto longest-valid-chain resolution allows an attacker or a runaway test loop possessing a valid principal key to flood the ledger with cheap G0 or G3 verdicts, establish a longer branch, and cause the audit replay to quarantine legitimate historical verdicts. A single-writer ledger detecting a fork must fail closed, quarantine both branches, and halt routing authority immediately.

#### Rank 2: Section 4.1 (Selection)
- Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE
- Exact wording that fails: "eff_lb95 = w * lb95 + (1 - w) * 0.5 with age_days since last_verdict_utc, p0 = 0.5 pessimistic prior. Decay only demotes; freshness is re-earned by new verdicts"
- Damning evidence:
  1. The statement "Decay only demotes" is mathematically false. If a failing model has lb95 < 0.5 (for example, lb95 = 0.15 after failing 20 of 20 tasks), as age_days increases, w approaches 0 and eff_lb95 moves toward 0.5. At age_days = half_life_days, w = 0.5, producing eff_lb95 = (0.5 * 0.15) + (0.5 * 0.5) = 0.325. Decay actively promotes failing models toward the 0.5 prior.
  2. The calculation "with age_days since last_verdict_utc" relies on a single scalar timestamp per cell (Section 2 `capability.last_verdict_utc`). If a cell contains 500 stale verdicts from 180 days ago, a single new verdict today sets age_days = 0, returning w to 1.0 and resetting decay across the entire historical corpus.

#### Rank 3: Section 4.3 (Escalation decision boundaries)
- Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE
- Exact wording that fails: "P(fail_i) * (C_rework + price_j) > price_j + P(fail_j) * C_rework, with P(fail) = 1 - eff_lb95 (ledger estimate, not self-confidence) and C_rework a MEASURED constant from the acceptance harness rework data."
- Damning evidence:
  1. The arithmetic completely omits price_i (the execution price of the cheaper tier model i). The expected cost of routing to tier i first is price_i + P(fail_i) * (price_j + C_rework). The cost of jumping directly to higher tier j is price_j + P(fail_j) * C_rework. Omitting price_i evaluates escalation economics as if candidate model i executes for free.
  2. Trigger T4 mandates: "eff_lb95 < threshold while raw lb95 >= threshold (decay demotion): do NOT climb; ship current-tier answer flagged stale: true and schedule the forced probe." If eff_lb95 < threshold, model i failed qualification under Section 4.1 rule 3 ("eff_lb95 >= threshold"). Trigger T4 forces the router to dispatch an answer from a disqualified model, violating the routing boundary established in Section 4.1.

THREE WEAKEST SECTIONS, ranked by damage if unfixed

1. Section 3.1 G3 CAP, with AMENDMENT 6  
Verdict: KILL. The hard rule as written is trivially bypassable.  
Exact wording that fails: Section 3.1 says "at least one G0/G1/G2 verdict is required before a cell may qualify." AMENDMENT 6 implements this as "n_non_g3 = ... >= 1."  
Evidence that damns it: Section 3.1 weight table gives G3 weight 0.25 and marks it "CAPPED." AMENDMENT 6 says the cap is "a composition gate on qualification, not a claim about the eff_lb95 arithmetic." A cell with 1 G0 pass and 999 G3 passes has weighted passes = 1 + 0.25 * 999 = 250.75, weighted fails = 0, pass_rate_raw near 1.0, and a high pass_rate_lb95. It qualifies. The cap does not cap G3 influence; it caps only all-G3 cells. One G0 verdict unlocks unlimited G3 volume.

2. Section 2 DDL, Section 3.1 weighted update, and Section 4.1 selection  
Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE. The statistical foundation is invalid.  
Exact wording that fails: Section 2 says "pass_rate_lb95 REAL NOT NULL, -- Wilson lower bound (routing)." Section 3.1 says "pass_rate_raw = sum(w*v)/sum(w); passes/fails accumulate weights; sample_size counts raw verdicts." AMENDMENT 6 says "pass_rate_lb95 by the section 2 Wilson formula on the weighted counts."  
Evidence that damns it: Section 2 defines the Wilson formula with p and n, which assumes integer counts from independent Bernoulli trials. Section 3.1 assigns weights G0 = 1.0, G1 = 1.0, G2 = 0.5, G3 = 0.25. The DDL stores passes and fails as REAL. Weighted counts are not integer trial counts, and weighted verdicts are not independent Bernoulli trials of equal weight. The reported 95 percent lower bound is not a valid Wilson bound for the underlying pass probability.

3. Section 4.3 T2 ECONOMICS  
Verdict: KEEP-WITH-REWRITE. The probability estimate is a category error.  
Exact wording that fails: "P(fail) = 1 - eff_lb95 (ledger estimate, not self-confidence)."  
Evidence that damns it: Section 1 defines eff_lb95 as a decay-blended Wilson 95 percent lower bound. Section 4.1 defines eff_lb95 = w * lb95 + (1 - w) * 0.5 with p0 = 0.5 pessimistic prior. A lower confidence bound is not a point estimate of failure probability. Using 1 - eff_lb95 as P(fail) systematically overstates failure for high-n cells because eff_lb95 is below the raw pass rate by construction. T2 is advisory while C_rework is unmeasured, but once C_rework is set from harness rework data, T2 will climb on a statistically wrong P(fail).
